correctness.rationale: The claim is reconstructed from Definition 1.3 for \(n=11\) and \(L=(1,2,3,5)\). Exact boundary ranks are \(10,44,65\); explicit maximal-rank minors have determinants \(1,-1,1\), proving torsion-free homology with ranks \((1,1,1,1)\). A complete acyclic matching on one vertex link leaves one critical \(0\)-cell and three critical \(2\)-cells; cyclic translation makes all vertex links isomorphic. A second implementation reproduced the face vector and modular ranks before packaging.

value.rationale: This is the unique all-distinct four-length vector at the next possible total length after the previously recorded smallest nongeneric case. Its behavior is structurally different: the whole complex has the integral homology of \(S^1\times S^2\), yet every vertex link is \(\bigvee^3S^2\). This is a natural boundary datum for understanding why genericity is needed and shows that global homology alone can hide severe local singularity.
